**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Execute the memory CLI only from a trusted checkout**

When this script is invoked from a PR or detached review worktree, `root` comes from the caller's current checkout and this line runs that checkout's `.claude/hooks/contextdb_cli.py`, allowing a PR that modifies the file to execute arbitrary code on the orchestrator host. `uv run --help` describes `uv run` as running a command or script and says `--no-project` only avoids project/workspace discovery, so that flag does not establish trust. Resolve the CLI from the trusted script/main checkout or verify the checkout before execution; the environment residual in the threat table does not mitigate this PR-controlled-code path.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/61290da8801cd714788814a6a6d077a37773a044/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

Split the row per script or reference tests that actually close every risk covered by this broad control.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject files with multiple trailing newlines**

When the line file contains a valid message followed by one or more blank lines, Bash command substitution strips all trailing newline characters before the check on line 34, so this accepts a multi-line file and dispatches only its first nonblank line despite the stated exactly-one-line contract. Preserve a sentinel while reading or otherwise validate the file's physical line count before stripping the single permitted terminator.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record the dispatched line in the acceptance record**

Once the pending playbook-rules change is enabled, every TASK, ACCEPTANCE, and PING sent through this script is expected to be recorded under the current acceptance record's `dispatch:` key with its bus/read evidence (`.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T128-playbook-rules-a04.md`, item 1), but the script accepts no record path and this final action only invokes `agmsg-dispatch`. Consequently every successful dispatch omits the evidence that the new procedure relies on to report a seat as working, even though this task says landing these scripts makes that rule true.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the TASK hash before dispatching**

When an `AGMSG-TASK` omits `task_sha256=`, this loop has no matching token, reaches the final `exec`, and sends a task whose file was never authenticated. This defeats the repository invariant that every task dispatch is hash-bound and can let a worker act on mutable task contents before the later merge gate detects the omission; require `task_file=` and a valid `task_sha256=` for TASK messages before checking any optional hashes. The threat table's closed test exercises only a present-but-wrong hash, so it does not close this omission path.
